- When sentiment is negative (e.g., -0.25) in the recent history, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- Model consistently underestimates late-period price spikes (especially 20-30 day horizon) — apply a “late spike bias” correction: add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for days 25–30 if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- Model overreacts to early sentiment shifts (e.g., sudden +0.50) by overshooting downward — dampen initial forecast drop by 0.3–0.7% if sentiment turns positive.
- Mean reversion bias: model often overcorrects from recent highs/lows — apply a 0.5–1.0% smoothing factor toward historical 10-day average for mid-to-late horizon.
- If sentiment is flat (0.00) for 3+ consecutive days, model tends to drift downward — add 0.2–0.5% upward bias to prevent premature decline.
